classification_reasons: Blast radius: plugin/gate/checks.py's lesson_and_eval/_supersedes_problem gates every entry_route:incident change at gate (e) for every project on this plugin version going forward; this change also ships a new generated-index subsystem (plugin/lessons/index.py) and edits docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md's contract text -- several independent, load-bearing pieces of behavior, not a small patch.

The spec reopened one concern mid-review (the Windows newline/CRLF mechanism) and this phase's own fix rounds surfaced a process defect (a double iteration bump past the non-routine cap) that needed an owner label to clear -- not a tight, single-pass spec.

New, previously-uncovered code paths (supersedes path/shape validation added in PR #132, frontmatter bad-field-shape handling) were added with new tests in recent rounds, which is exactly the kind of change existing tests did not already cover before this change.
attempted: Intent: round 4's stated purpose (apply the owner's sdlc:reset-iterations, re-check the two still-open PR review threads, conclude items 1-3 already landed and items 4-9 remain the owner's explicit 'can wait for 0.3.7' deferral) matches intent.md/spec.md's scope and the prior rounds' documented decisions; no drift.

Spec and plan: unchanged this round; spec.md and plan.md already carry every requirement and fail case from prior rounds (verified against their own citations); no new requirement introduced, none left undecided (all Flagged concerns in spec.md are [x]).

Proof -- re-review of the specific prior escalation: compared the rewritten fix-response.md Round 4 section against evidence/hook-log.jsonl. The log does show three real Edit-tool invocations at 2026-10-08T11:38:30-37Z on plugin/gate/artifacts.py, plugin/gate/checks.py and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md, exactly as my prior verdict found. The rewritten text now candidly admits this (drafted items 8/9's wording fixes, then reverted with `git checkout --`). I independently verified the claim rather than taking it on faith: (a) the current on-disk/diffed text of plugin/gate/artifacts.py:89 still reads '...lesson and eval (change 0003...' (the exact 'eval (' shape items 8/9 would have reworded), (b) plugin/gate/checks.py:1637's docstring still reads '...its lesson and its eval (spec.md change 0003)', and (c) diff-e.patch's docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md hunk still reads 'a heading per tag' (not the drafted 'a heading per class'/'eval case' rewording) -- all three files read as if the edits never landed, which is what a genuine revert-before-commit produces. The owner's own review text (fix-requests.json, review #5452163356 item 8) independently confirms these are the same two 'eval (' comments and marks them optional/advisory, not blocking any test (the one test that did break on this pattern, test_security_baseline_check_finds_secrets_and_dangerous_calls, scans an /sdlc-init-initialized fixture built from template/ content, not plugin/gate/*.py comments, so these two deferred comments do not in fact fail any test in the suite). build/test/lint logs correctly still read 'deferred to the runner' (no code change this round); verifier.md is an earlier round's (00ddfc7) report, appropriate to leave standing since round 4 touched no code it exercised.

Blast radius: no guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, this repo's root sdlc.yaml) touched. template/sdlc.yaml and docs/OPERATING_MODEL.md are plugin-shipped/process-documentation content per plan.md's own citation and REVIEW.md's exception for a framework change (intent.md: 'Framework change: yes'), not this repository's own guardrails. No sdlc.yaml risk_list item applies (no auth, no money movement, no production-config path, no data migration).

Policies: REVIEW.md's framework rules are addressed -- plan.md/spec.md reflect the diff; the second-occurrence CLAUDE.md-entry rule's four findings (review-response.md, claude-md-proposals.md) are pre-existing, owner-deferred nits the prior round already handled correctly (proposed, not silently fixed, not self-edited into CLAUDE.md). No new stored personal/sensitive field. Definition-of-done: the deterministic gate check stays the enforcement; eval-case content quality stays advisory, as spec.md's Flagged concerns already settled.

Tests: no pre-existing test was weakened; this round added no test and claims no code change, consistent with the hook-log edits being reverted rather than landed (a real, untested edit to checks.py/artifacts.py would itself be a definition-of-done violation, which is exactly why this needed checking rather than taking the narrative at face value).
